description:
FILED s515c (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-11) from the HTTP-Tiny-0.090-0 board census.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s515c/pr/pblock.pl):
    my $fh = \*STDOUT;
    print({$fh} "a", "b", "\n") || die "x";      # perl: ab   PCL: PCL: statement dropped ... Missing case: ['Statement::Compound<{$fh}>','Statement::Expression<"a", "b", "\n">']
    print {$fh} "c\n";                            # both: c
    my @l = ("d", "\n"); print({$fh} @l);         # perl: d    PCL: dropped
PPI builds the `{$fh}` inside the call parens as a Statement::Compound followed by a Statement::Expression; the print-filehandle machinery (`_is_print_term_start` family) handles the paren-less spelling only.  Likely a PPI repair or a `print(` arm that re-reads `( {BLOCK} LIST )` as the block-filehandle form (rule 11: route into the existing block-filehandle path; printf/say share it).

REACH: HTTP-Tiny t/Util.pm line 46 (`print({$fh} @_) || die ...` in tmpfile) -- 020_headers.t (perl 5 rows) and 030_response.t (6) produce no rows.

=== DONE (s516a) ===
PPI bug (ppi-upstream-bugs.md section 37; report rows 88-89; canary misc-fixes-02.t): two wrong shapes -- Compound{Block} + a second statement (print, say), or the block as a Constructor followed by a term (printf, CORE::say).  Pl::Parser::_repair_paren_block_filehandle (in-place, text unchanged; _ppi_parse + fragment_doc) hands both to the existing paren-form path (_extract_paren_filehandle).  print({a=>1}) stays a hash.  Note: perl itself rejects print({$fh}) (syntax error), so that brief row was not added.  Drops: HTTP-Tiny t/Util.pm 1 -> 0, Path-Tiny lib/Path/Tiny.pm 2 -> 0 (the census populations had none).  Guard Pl/t/print-block-fh-01.t (10).  Commit fe4f3c5e (s516a).  The board rows stay behind #1575.
